title: RunService.RenderStepped
summary: Client-only event firing just before each rendered frame — the only place guaranteed to sync with what the player sees. Camera updates and aim smoothing live here. Never on the server.

details.heading: Client only
details.body: Never fires on the server (there's no rendering). Code guarded by RenderStepped connections must be client-reachable.

details.heading: Frame-critical
details.body: Work here directly delays the frame being drawn — heavy RenderStepped handlers visibly drop FPS. Also consider BindToRenderStep with priorities.

explanation.whatItIs: The last possible moment before pixels: perfect for anything that must align with the visible frame.
explanation.whyItExists: Camera math done in Heartbeat can lag one frame behind rendering; RenderStepped removes that gap.
whenToUse: Anything measured against 'what the player sees right now'
whenNotToUse: Gameplay state changes (keep those in Heartbeat or events)
Heavy computation — it taxes the frame directly
tips: BindToRenderStep for ordered camera systems with named priorities
Don't mix RenderStepped movement with physics simulation of the same object
commonMistakes: Connecting RenderStepped in a Script (server) and wondering why it never fires
Doing expensive work every frame 'because it's smooth'
Forgetting to scale by dt like everywhere else

examples.title: Camera look-at smoothing
examples.code:
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
local target = workspace.Beacon

local conn
conn = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function(dt)
    local current = camera.CFrame
    local goal = CFrame.lookAt(current.Position, target.Position)
    camera.CFrame = current:Lerp(goal, math.min(1, dt * 5))
end)

-- later: conn:Disconnect()
